name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
description: OpenThoughts3-1.2M is a 1.2 million example open-source dataset for training reasoning models, covering math, code, and science domains. It is the result of systematic investigation of each step of a data generation pipeline with 1,000+ controlled experiments. The dataset contains 850,000 math, 250,000 code, and 100,000 science datapoints, generated using QwQ-32B as the teacher model. Fine-tuning Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on this dataset yields OpenThinker3-7B, achieving state-of-the-art results on AIME 2025, LiveCodeBench, and GPQA Diamond.
license: Multiple licenses apply to source datasets; see Appendix Q for details. Key sources include Apache 2.0 (Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, QwQ-32B), CC-BY-4.0 (OpenCodeReasoning, Open2Math), CC-BY-SA-4.0 (StackExchange datasets).
creator: OpenThoughts Team (Etash Guha, Ryan Marten, Sedrick Keh, Negin Raoof, Georgios Smymis, and many others from Stanford University, University of Washington, BespokeLabs.ai, Toyota Research Institute, UC Berkeley, UT Austin, UCLA, LAION, NYU, UNC Chapel Hill, ASU, and other institutions)
citeAs: Guha, E., Marten, R., Keh, S., Raoof, N., Smymis, G., et al. (2025). Data Recipes for Reasoning Models. arXiv:2506.04178.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed through a multi-stage pipeline: (1) sourcing questions from existing datasets and newly generated datasets across math, code, and science domains; (2) mixing questions from top-performing sources; (3) filtering for high-quality questions using LLM-based methods (difficulty-based or response-length-based); (4) deduplicating questions and sampling multiple answers per question (16x); (5) generating answers using a teacher model (QwQ-32B); and (6) no answer filtering was applied as it did not improve performance. Over 1,000 controlled ablation experiments informed each pipeline design choice.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Web Scraping, Experiments, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No explicit discussion of missing data in the dataset. Some question sources produced fewer datapoints than required, in which case questions were repeated until the desired amount was reached.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions were sourced from 27 code sources (e.g., StackExchange CodeGolf, OpenCodeReasoning, KodCode-V1), 21 math sources (e.g., OpenMath-2-Math, NuminaMath-1.5, MathPile), and 14 science sources (e.g., StackExchange Physics, Organic Chemistry PDFs, CQADupStack-Physics). Sources include online forums, competition sites (CodeForces, AoPS, StackOverflow), LLM-generated synthetic datasets, and human-written question sets. Answers (reasoning traces) were generated using QwQ-32B as the teacher model.
rai:dataImputationProtocol: For question sources that produced fewer datapoints than required (31,600 per experiment), questions were repeated until the desired amount was reached.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions were filtered using LLM-based methods: difficulty-based filtering with GPT-4o-mini for code questions, and response-length filtering with GPT-4.1-mini for math and science questions. Questions were deduplicated using exact match deduplication for math and science, and no deduplication for code. Multiple answers (16x) were sampled per question from the teacher model QwQ-32B. Datasets were decontaminated against evaluation benchmarks using Normalized Indel similarity (75% threshold) and N-gram similarity (N=13) methods.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Pipeline steps: (1) Question sourcing from 62 total sources across math, code, and science. (2) Question mixing: top 1-2 sources per domain selected. (3) Question filtering: difficulty-based (GPT-4o-mini) for code; response-length-based (GPT-4.1-mini) for math and science. (4) Deduplication: exact deduplication for math and science; no deduplication for code. (5) Random sampling to target counts. (6) Answer generation: 16 answers per question using QwQ-32B. (7) No answer filtering applied. (8) Decontamination against evaluation benchmarks using Indel similarity and N-gram overlap. Final dataset: 850K math, 250K code, 100K science datapoints (1.2M total).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Answers (reasoning traces) were generated by teacher models (primarily QwQ-32B, with earlier versions using DeepSeek-R1). Each question was annotated 16 times by sampling from the teacher model with temperature=0.7, top_p=1.0, max_new_tokens=32,768. For question filtering, GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4.1-mini/nano were used to assess difficulty or generate responses for length-based selection. For earlier dataset versions (OpenThoughts-114K), answer verification used answer matching, unit tests, and LLM judges against ground truth.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: DeepSeek API (for DeepSeek-R1 annotations during pipeline experiments), QwQ-32B (for final OpenThoughts3 annotations), GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4.1-mini/nano (for question filtering and verification tasks). LlamaFactory was used as the training framework.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Extensive ablation experiments (1,000+) were conducted to evaluate annotation strategies. Key findings: (1) QwQ-32B outperforms DeepSeek-R1 as a teacher despite scoring lower on benchmarks. (2) No answer filtering strategy outperformed training on all samples. (3) Sampling 16 answers per question provides effective data scaling. (4) Verification methods (majority consensus, GPT verification, unit tests) did not significantly improve downstream performance. (5) Removing self-reflection from reasoning traces caused a 49.1% relative performance drop.
rai:annotationsPerItem: 16 answers (reasoning traces) generated per question by the teacher model (QwQ-32B).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: QwQ-32B (primary teacher model for answer generation), DeepSeek-R1 (teacher model used in pipeline experiments and earlier dataset versions), GPT-4o-mini (question difficulty filtering, question filtering, verification tasks), GPT-4.1-mini (response-length-based question filtering for math and science), GPT-4.1-nano (response-length-based question filtering), Gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05 (OCR for organic chemistry PDFs), FastText classifiers (question and answer filtering), OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (embedding-based filtering), Evalchemy (evaluation framework)
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is released as part of the OpenThoughts project with iterative releases (BespokeStratos-17K, OpenThoughts-114K, OpenThoughts2-1M, OpenThoughts3-1.2M). Assets are hosted on Hugging Face at https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-thoughts/OpenThoughts3-1.2M. Codebase is available at https://github.com/open-thoughts/open-thoughts. No explicit deprecation policy stated.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables open-source development of reasoning models competitive with proprietary systems, democratizing access to high-quality reasoning model training data. However, safety analysis shows that supervised fine-tuning on reasoning data inadvertently degrades safety alignment: OpenThinker3-7B achieves a harmfulness rate of 55.5% on HarmBench compared to 14.5% for the base Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct model. The authors acknowledge this trade-off between reasoning capability and safety, and note that future work should incorporate safety-specific datasets.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset focuses exclusively on math, code, and science domains, which may limit generalization to other reasoning domains. Question sources are predominantly English-language. The pipeline selects top-performing question sources (top 1-2 per domain), which may introduce source-specific biases. No explicit analysis of demographic or cultural biases in the question content is provided.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to math, code, and science domains; reinforcement learning datasets are not explored. The pipeline was optimized for average benchmark performance across domains rather than per-domain optimization, which may not be optimal for specialized use cases. Out-of-domain transfer gains observed during pipeline experiments disappear when in-domain data is mixed in. Some benchmarks (AMC23, MATH500) show saturation at the largest scales. The dataset does not include safety-specific or alignment-focused data, leading to degraded safety performance in trained models. CommonCrawl does not appear to contain long reasoning traces similar to those used by current reasoning models.
rai:dataUseCases: Primary use case: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) of language models to develop reasoning capabilities in math, code, and science. The dataset is designed for training reasoning models that generate long chains of thought. It can be used to fine-tune base models (demonstrated with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct). Not recommended for: reinforcement learning training (dataset not designed for this), safety-critical applications without additional safety tuning, or domains outside math, code, and science.
